Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; please know I will guide you through a few quick questions to understand your symptoms better. 

To start, how many days old is the baby, and did you notice any fever, vomiting, or changes in breathing pattern like grunting or flaring nostrils?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

Based on the history of prematurity (33 weeks) and early-onset respiratory distress, this is highly suggestive of RDS due to surfactant deficiency. I am proceeding with a diagnosis based on the strong clinical correlation between the patient's gestational age and symptoms.
